chunk_findings.detail: The capture path unconditionally uses a process-wide `RUSAGE_CHILDREN` before/after delta even on Linux/macOS where `wait4` is available, because it calls `R.measure(None, before)` instead of metering the child directly. `RUSAGE_CHILDREN` is global to the whole ddflow process, so any child reaped by another thread or by unrelated code during the capture is charged to this command. For example, if thread A calls `capture(["python", "-c", "print(1)"])` while thread B runs and reaps a CPU-heavy child, thread A’s `Captured.resources.cpu_user_s` can include thread B’s child. The same snapshot is also invalid for peak RSS: `RUSAGE_CHILDREN.ru_maxrss` is a monotonic high-water mark over all waited-for children, not a per-interval peak. After one child peaks at 500 MB, a later command that peaks at 10 MB will yield a maxrss delta of 0 (or 500 MB if the code uses the after value), so `maxrss_kb` is not the command’s peak RSS.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/proc.py:capture

chunk_findings.detail: The new metering is attached to the direct child created by `popen(command, cls=MeteredPopen, shell=True, ...)`, which is the shell process, not the full gate-command tree. For an input such as `run_shell("sleep 5 | cat")`, or any command that spawns helper processes, the metered PID is `/bin/sh`; `wait4` on that PID returns only the shell’s own resources (often near zero), and the descendants’ CPU, RSS, and block I/O are not included. Starting the command in a process group does not make kernel `rusage` aggregate a process tree, so the resulting `cpu_user_s`, `maxrss_kb`, and I/O fields can be materially wrong for the actual gate command.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/proc.py:_run_shell

chunk_findings.detail: In the timeout path, `_note_cost` is called only after `kill_group(p)` and `_drain(p)`, and only when `p.returncode is not None`. For a standard `subprocess.Popen`, `returncode` becomes non-`None` only after `Popen.wait()`/`poll()` has already reaped the child via `os.waitpid`; once that has happened, `os.wait4()` cannot retrieve that child's rusage (it will fail with `ChildProcessError`). If `_drain` does not reap the child, `p.returncode` remains `None` and `_note_cost` silently records nothing. Thus a timed-out gate command cannot produce the intended per-child `wait4` evidence: either no `Resources` are appended, or the implementation must fall back to the process-wide `RUSAGE_CHILDREN` before/after delta. That delta is not per-child attribution: for example, if another ddflow child is running or is waited for during the interval, its CPU/RSS can be charged to the timed-out command; if the timed-out child was not properly reaped by this process, its usage can be omitted entirely. This violates the stated requirement that `wait4` provide the child's own user/system CPU, maxrss, and block I/O, with delta only when `wait4` is genuinely unusable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/proc.py:_note_cost

chunk_findings.detail: The fake rusage tests hard-code Linux units but do not control the platform. On macOS (`sys.platform == "darwin"`), `ru_maxrss` is bytes and the change is required to normalise it to KB; `_ru()` sets `ru_maxrss=2048`, so a compliant `R.from_rusage(_ru())` should produce `maxrss_kb == 2`, not `2048`. The same assumption breaks `test_measure_prefers_wait4_then_delta_then_unavailable`, where fake `ru_maxrss=4096` becomes 4 KB on macOS, so the assertion `d.maxrss_kb == 4096` fails. These tests will fail on a supported macOS run unless they monkeypatch the platform or use platform-appropriate raw values.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_resource_capture.py:test_from_rusage_fake_gives_the_evidence_fields

chunk_findings.detail: The real-child tests interpolate `sys.executable` directly into a shell string without quoting. If the Python executable path contains spaces (for example `[REDACTED:path] Doe/.venv/bin/python`), the command becomes `[REDACTED:path] Doe/.venv/bin/python -c '...'`, which the shell parses as program `[REDACTED:path]` with extra arguments. The child never starts, `r.ok` is false, and the resource-capture tests fail. The tests should quote `sys.executable` (e.g. `shlex.quote`).
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_resource_capture.py:test_real_child_that_allocates_and_burns_cpu_is_measured

chunk_findings.detail: This test asserts that a normal POSIX `P.capture([sys.executable, "-c", "print(1)"], timeout=20)` reports `resources_source == "delta"`. The stated intent requires `capture` to use per-child `wait4` when it is usable and to fall back to a delta only when `wait4` is not usable. On normal Linux/macOS, a compliant `capture` should therefore report `wait4`; this test either fails against the correct implementation or locks in an implementation that never uses `wait4` for capture.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_resource_capture.py:test_capture_reports_an_approximate_delta

chunk_findings.detail: The burn fixture allocates 150 MB and the real-child test requires peak RSS of at least 140 MB. In a memory-constrained but otherwise supported environment (for example a container with a 128 MB cgroup limit, or several pytest-xdist workers sharing a small container), `bytearray(150 * 1024 * 1024)` raises `MemoryError`, `r.ok` becomes false, and the resource-capture tests fail. The allocation size should be adaptive, configurable, or skipped when the process cannot allocate enough memory.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_resource_capture.py:_BURN

chunk_findings.detail: `resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN.ru_maxrss` is a high-water mark over all previously reaped children in the process, not a per-child delta. The code sets `ru_maxrss = after.ru_maxrss`, so when wait4 is unusable and an earlier child had a larger peak RSS, that previous child’s peak is attributed to the current command. Example: child A ran with a 1 GiB peak and was waited normally; later child B is run with SIGCHLD ignored, so wait4 fails. The before and after `children_snapshot()` values both still carry A’s 1 GiB high-water mark, and B’s evidence records `maxrss_kb=1048576` even if B used 2 MiB. Because the field is recorded as `maxrss_kb` while only the imperfect `resources_source=delta` hints it may be approximate, this is wrong per-command peak RSS data.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/resources.py:110 `_delta`

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `res.cpu_user_s + res.cpu_sys_s >= 0.35` is wrong for the wait4 path. `P.run_shell(f"{sys.executable} -c '{_BURN}' & wait")` executes `/bin/sh -c 'python -c <burn> & wait'`; the direct child of `ddflow` is the shell, and the Python process that burns 0.4s is a grandchild. `wait4` on the direct shell child reports only the shell's own `ru_utime`/`ru_stime` (a few milliseconds), not the background child's CPU. This same test file relies on `P.run_shell` reaping the shell via `P.MeteredPopen` (see line 117), so normal execution of this input will produce far below 0.35 and the test fails.
